admission.authority: direct user continuation of the BRC >100 multiplier-horizon attack after pairwise transport and kernel-compression falsification
admission.reason: Prove and execute a certified table-free short-step multiplier tail using exact alternating binomial lower bounds, reducing long-horizon predictor-table dependence without claiming a faster Python factor scan.

methods.name: BRC table-free certified multiplier tail
capabilities: exact h=1,2 root/remainder transport with no sqrt-ratio predictor table when certified
arbitrary even-order alternating half-binomial lower predictor
exact integer certificate for at most two BRC basin corrections
tail frontier scaling O(N^(1/(2K+1))) for fixed even degree K
explicit CPU-negative benchmark boundary for current Python implementation
methods.core_law: For x=h/m in (0,1] and even K, the alternating binomial truncation L_K(x) is below sqrt(1+x)-1 and its error is at most binom(1/2,K+1)x^(K+1). Thus d=floor(J L_K) is a lower root-increment predictor. If binom(1/2,K+1) J (h/m)^(K+1)+h/(2m)<=1, then at most two odd BRC basin crossings recover the exact (m+h) root/remainder state.
methods.hard_boundary: Storage/predictor-dependence result, not a Python performance win. High-order exact polynomial evaluation was slower than optimized isqrt in the finite benchmark. It does not reduce the multiplier search count, does not change Hart/Lehman asymptotic factorization complexity, does not establish RSA-scale practicality, and does not modify Foundation state.
